product_from_film: Reframe in Reve changes image framing, zoom and aspect ratio.
explains_well: The same picnic poster and house scene visibly change from narrow to wide formats.
unclear: The samples do not establish image quality at full resolution or how unseen image areas are created.
scenario: Reframe a city image and adapt a picnic poster from portrait to landscape.
product_clear_basis: The change-aspect-ratios label at 10s leads through an editor to a visibly wider version of the same picnic poster at 16s.

scenes.action: Zoom in text sits beside Earth, then a regional image and city view. The city fills the frame, appears in an editor and changes to a closer bridge view.
scenes.design: White/black fields, rounded image card and clean sans-serif text.
scenes.purpose: Introduce zoom and connect it to image editing.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–10s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Change Aspect Ratios introduces a portrait picnic poster in the editor. Side settings appear; the poster then fills a landscape composition with related text and decoration.
scenes.design: Purple/gold illustrated poster, white editor and small toolbar.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 10–17s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: From Vertical and To Horizontal accompany a house image and ratio icons. A wide house row carries Try Reframe, then a picnic scene appears in front.
scenes.design: Translucent ratio selector and broad landscape image.
scenes.purpose: Repeat the benefit with photographic-looking material.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 17–23s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A top-down picnic becomes smaller in grass; city and regional views follow with Now on Reve, ending on Earth.
scenes.design: Green field, aerial city and blue planet.
scenes.purpose: Reverse the opening scale idea and close the loop.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 23–30.53s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Zoom introduction leads to editor proof, poster format change, photo format change and an outward scale ending.
Zoom in text and Earth grow across 0–2s; the scale motif is explicit but the product context comes later.
Image creators adapting formats are implied by the editor and poster. The full task is clear at the 16s wide-poster result.
Successive Earth/region/city and picnic/field/city states imply inward and outward scaling. Exact continuous zoom path is unverified.
The image-to-editor change gives a functional anchor between scale sequences. Portrait and landscape poster states are visible, but the transformation mechanism is unresolved.
Plain white fields keep attention on detailed images and the purple/gold poster. The translucent ratio selector is a decorative UI layer.
Large Zoom in, Change Aspect Ratios and Vertical/Horizontal text states make benefits explicit. Small editor settings are not needed for the broad explanation.
Voice delivery is unverified.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Earth/aerial imagery, city houses and an illustrated poster are used. Their sources and generation methods are not known.
Source duration 30.53 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: The aspect-ratio task is clear silently because the same poster and houses recur in new shapes.
Central images and surrounding whitespace create a stable focus. Ratio outlines reinforce the requested shape.
Two related functions fit into 30s; the poster example gives the strongest concrete result. The globe travel is less necessary for practical understanding.
The opening zoom promise returns in reverse at the end, while middle examples give a usable framing benefit.
The wide range of scale appears intended to create wonder and control; viewer response is not measured.
The city setting, picnic theme and Earth start/end give unusually strong continuity across feature examples.
Matching portrait/wide outputs and editor states are visible. Resolution, text fidelity and real generation behavior are not independently tested.
The scale loop and city/picnic world unify the film. The clean UI style alone is not brand-specific.
The poster transformation directly explains utility. One less scale montage would allow a closer comparison of preserved content.
For Tin multi-channel campaigns, show one poster adapting to two channel sizes while retaining its headline and key information.
categories.experiment: Put before/after versions side by side and mark the unchanged headline.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Use the same detailed poster in both formats so the change is immediately inspectable.
try: For Tin, adapt one campaign poster to portrait and landscape while keeping the same headline, date and product image visible.
Build a short scale-loop opening/ending around one campaign asset, with the actual editor action in the middle.
lessons.avoid: Letting impressive scale changes replace a full-resolution check of the adapted output.
lessons.open: Image fidelity, actual edit behavior, unseen-area generation, sound and precise zoom path remain unverified.

comparison.story: Zoom promise → editor → poster ratio change → house ratio change → outward scale loop.
comparison.motion: Scale and format state changes; continuous paths not resolved.
comparison.sound: No validated listening or synchronization check.
comparison.texture: Clean white layouts, detailed poster and photographic-looking city imagery.
comparison.lesson: Matched before/after content is stronger proof than a generic feature claim.
